clue.text: A dampener when the pub's out of whisky, say ?

definitions.text: A dampener when the pub's out of whisky, say

parts.words: A dampener when the pub's out of whisky, say
parts.note: a fine Highland drizzle is a dampener; and a pub whose whisky has run out has the spirit from north of the border missed, which said quickly gives the same phrase

explanation.surface: A drinker's gloom on finding the bar has run dry of whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is a fine wet drizzle in Scotland; read as a sound-alike it is 'Scotch missed', what a whiskyless pub leaves you with.
explanation.definitionFit: The drizzle typical of the Highlands literally dampens anyone out in it.

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a bear is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: on the stock exchange a bear sells shares, expecting prices to fall

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is space to keep a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The bear is not an animal but a speculator who sells; SELLER spoken sounds like the underground storeroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground storage room beneath a house.

indicators.note: rough means the letters of path are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England (several share the name)

explanation.surface: A rough path down to a riverside inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' turns PATH into TAPH; the OUSE is a river in Yorkshire and another in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub where beer is drawn from the tap is an inn or alehouse.

definitions.meaning: determined to have one's own way, obstinate
read literally, having a powerful brain or mind

explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate people go their own way; split in two the word suggests a mighty intellect.

indicators.note: could be means these letters could be rearranged into another word

parts.note: Smike, the wretched boy in Dickens's Nicholas Nickleby, and the word or, run together in the held text

explanation.surface: Life is dreary for poor Smike, or at least it could be.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'Smike—or'; 'could be' rearranges SMIKE plus OR. Smike is the ill-treated pupil at Dotheboys Hall in Nicholas Nickleby.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that irks annoys by being wearisome.

annotationWithheld.why: Ruler turns up right away (4): the answer is a Russian ruler, but no reading of 'turns up right away' yields those letters

clue.text: Possibly the Argo's carrying a ship load of sea-weed

indicators.note: carrying means the rearranged letters hold the next part inside them
possibly means the letters of Argo's might be arranged another way

parts.note: the possessive is read as the letters ARGOS
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Jason's Argo hauling a cargo of seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo is Jason's ship in Greek myth, which suits the surface; here its name is only letters to rearrange, and 'carrying' makes them wrap round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sargassum is a floating brown alga, giving its name to the weed-choked sea.

clue.text: Pansy takes comfort after the suit

indicators.note: after means the word for comfort comes following the suit

parts.note: hearts is a suit in a pack of cards
ease means comfort

explanation.surface: A flower given comfort after a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the suit' sounds legal, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild viola is a small flower of the violet family.

parts.note: a scrap is a small bit or fragment
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A fragment of a news report about trouble somewhere out east.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting into a scrape means landing in an embarrassing difficulty.

parts.note: the word names both a pancake cooked in a pan and a flat powder compact, the case of the surface

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether a fried treat is the right choice here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In this case' looks like 'in this instance', but a case is a container: the same name is used for a fried pancake and for a lady's flat powder compact.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat pancake cooked on a griddle is also the name for a slim compact holding face powder.

clue.text: The dog in the trap to the right

parts.note: a springe is an old word for a snare that catches small game

explanation.surface: A dog caught in a snare, seen off to the right.
explanation.walkthrough: A SPRINGE is a noose snare; adding R gives a breed of spaniel used to flush game.
explanation.definitionFit: This spaniel breed, English or Welsh, is a gundog that springs game from cover.

indicators.note: endless means the word for deception loses its final letter

parts.note: fraud is criminal deception

explanation.surface: A woman from abroad who keeps tricking people.
explanation.definitionFit: German for wife or Mrs, used in English for a German woman.

clue.text: Panic over act on dole reform ? Nonsense !

indicators.note: over means in this down clue the word for panic sits above the next part
on means the following part is attached after the word for act

parts.note: a flap is a state of panic
to do is to act

indicators.note: reform means the letters of dole are formed again in new order

explanation.surface: Alarm over a measure to reform unemployment benefit, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges DOLE into ODLE. The dole is British slang for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for balderdash or empty talk.

clue.text: Drummers collect many tips round the street

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation for street
collect means the letters of many tips are gathered up and put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Street drummers take in plenty of tips from passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collect' rearranges MANY TIPS into TYMPANIS, and 'round' puts it around ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of kettledrums in an orchestra are the percussionists who beat them.

parts.note: inspiration in its literal sense is breathing in, which needs air around you

explanation.surface: What a creative person needs before ideas arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' looks like creative spark, but it is the act of drawing breath, which requires air.
explanation.definitionFit: The air surrounding the earth is needed before anyone can breathe in.

clue.text: Bill takes bird on an infernal river

parts.note: AC (account) is a bill to be settled
the heron is a long-legged wading bird

explanation.surface: A bird takes on a river of hell, as in a fable.
explanation.walkthrough: AC, short for account, is a standard crossword way of saying bill.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this was one of the rivers of the underworld, crossed by Charon's ferry.

parts.note: ho is a call to attract attention
ads is short for advertisements

explanation.surface: Rash people cheer the adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash, quick-tempered individuals who act without thinking.

clue.text: Vessel going a mile an hour, oar being broken

parts.note: MPH is miles per hour

indicators.note: being broken means the letters of oar are smashed and set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A boat crawling along at a mile an hour because its oar has snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-handled jar of ancient Greece and Rome is a vessel for wine or oil.

parts.note: a large wine cask, whose name read as a pig's head suggests brawn, meat set in jelly from a boiled pig's head

explanation.surface: A strong man employed to carry wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brawny' looks like muscular; brawn is also a British jellied meat made from a pig's head, hence a hog's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask holding wine or beer, of about fifty imperial gallons.

clue.text: A psalm with opening bar preceding it

indicators.note: preceding means the opening passage comes before the word it

parts.note: an intro is the opening passage of a piece of music

explanation.surface: Music for a psalm with an introductory bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The chant or psalm sung as the priest enters at the start of Mass.

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
gents are men, male people

explanation.surface: A note on men being put off cleaning products.
explanation.definitionFit: Soapless washing agents are a class of cleaning product.

definitions.meaning: wild animals hunted for sport or food

explanation.definitionFit: A spirited person is willing to try; and hunted birds and beasts are called this collectively.

clue.text: This coil one associates with a Great Dane

definitions.text: This coil one associates with a Great Dane

parts.words: This coil one associates with a Great Dane
parts.note: Hamlet, the great Prince of Denmark, speaks of shuffling off this coil in his soliloquy

explanation.surface: A coiled lead that goes with a large dog breed.
explanation.walkthrough: A Great Dane looks like the dog, but it is Hamlet, whose 'To be or not to be' speech mentions the coil of earthly life.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective completes Shakespeare's phrase for the troubles of earthly existence.

parts.note: a boss who supervises others, read as someone tall enough to see over everyone's heads

explanation.surface: A question about a manager of great height.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as OVER-SEER, it is someone who sees over others, as a tall person can.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor watching workers is literally one who looks over them.

clue.text: Wear perhaps in which a Western gun-man appears

indicators.note: in which means the gunman's name lies inside the words wear perhaps

explanation.surface: A garment worn by a cowboy in a western film.
explanation.walkthrough: Wyatt Earp was the lawman of the gunfight at the OK Corral.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt of the OK Corral shoot-out is the famous lawman of the Wild West.

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of Poe are given a new order
unusual means the letters of treat come in an out-of-the-ordinary order

explanation.surface: An entertainment from a Poe novel would be an unusual treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' makes OPE from POE and 'unusual' makes RETTA from TREAT. 'Novel' looks like Poe's book, but it is an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera with spoken dialogue is a stage entertainment.

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: Someone agreeing that a book belongs on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: An account book records a business's transactions.
